note: Attacker-controlled first input byte sets the output buffer size multiplier.
Attacker-controlled second input byte multiplies the output buffer size; the product determines the malloc size.
Allocates an uninitialized heap buffer of attacker-controlled size; contents are indeterminate.
Passes the uninitialized buffer and the full attacker-controlled input to uncompress, which invokes the inflate path.
Entry point of the inflate loop; forwards the uninitialized output buffer and input bytes to tinfl_decompress.
Sets the output cursor to the start of the uninitialized malloc buffer and the end pointer to buffer start plus the attacker-controlled size.
Computes the wrapping mask from the output buffer size; with a small attacker-chosen buffer this mask is small, so dist indices wrap within the uninitialized region.
Enters the distance-copy loop with attacker-controlled counter (the match length) from the compressed stream.
Checks whether the output cursor has reached the end of the small attacker-sized buffer.
When the output buffer is full, the state machine saves counter and dist_from_out_buf_start and returns HAS_MORE_OUTPUT; on resume, case 53 re-enters the loop body.

Copies a byte from the output history; when dist exceeds the number of bytes written so far, the wrapped index reads from the uninitialized malloc region, and the value is then written back, propagating uninitialized data.
The read of uninitialized heap memory is the memory-safety sink; MSan flags the use of the indeterminate value copied into the output buffer.
